newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM, EXXON PLASTICS VENTURE IN PRODUCTION.
newsitem.headline: DSM, EXXON PLASTICS VENTURE IN PRODUCTION.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM said on Wednesday its 50-50 plastomers joint venture in the Netherlands with Exxon Chemical, had started commercial production.
"The product can now be released onto the market and pre-marketing indicates there will be pretty fast growth in demand," the venture's managing director Ger van der Horst said.

The venture, Dex Plastomers, was formed in May 1995 at DSM's Geleen site to produce a new generation of high-grade polymers which will eventually replace the traditional polymers also still being produced at the Geleen plants.
Van der Horst said output was roughly estimated to reach some 10-15,000 tonnes in the first year.
Depending on demand, total production capacity could rise to 120,000 tonnes per year, but this was many years away, he said.

Van der Horst said Dex Plastomers would target Europe, where the new polymers could be applied in a range of specialty markets such as flexible packaging, rotation moulding and wire and cable coating.
